title: SSH Hardening Basics
objectives: Harden network device SSH configuration by disabling Telnet, enabling SSH v2, and restricting access.
scenario: A network device is currently accessible via Telnet, which sends passwords in plaintext. You need to harden the device by enabling SSH v2 and disabling Telnet.
concepts: SSH v2 uses RSA for key exchange
Domain-name required for crypto key generation
transport input ssh restricts access to SSH only
login local requires local user database

errors.solution: Verify domain-name is configured and crypto keys are generated
Configure domain-name first, then generate keys with crypto key generate rsa

questions.question: Why is SSH preferred over Telnet?
questions.solution: SSH encrypts all traffic including passwords; Telnet sends everything in plaintext

steps.title: Configure Device Identity
steps.instruction: Set the device hostname and domain-name. These are prerequisites for generating RSA keys used by SSH.
steps.why: SSH requires a domain-name to generate crypto keys. Without it, you cannot enable SSH.
steps.expectedOutput: Hostname and domain-name configured
hints: Use 'hostname [name]' to set the device name

commonMistakes.mistake: Trying to generate keys before setting domain-name

steps.title: Generate RSA Crypto Keys
steps.instruction: Generate RSA key pair for SSH. This creates the encryption keys that secure SSH connections.
steps.why: SSH v2 uses RSA keys for key exchange and encryption. Without keys, SSH cannot operate.
steps.expectedOutput: RSA key generated
hints: Use 'crypto key generate rsa modulus 1024' or higher

steps.title: Enable SSH Version 2
steps.instruction: Configure the device to accept only SSH v2 connections. SSH v2 has improved security over v1.
steps.why: SSH v1 has known vulnerabilities. Always use SSH v2 when available.
steps.expectedOutput: SSH version 2 enabled
hints: Use 'ip ssh version 2' to enforce SSH v2

steps.title: Configure VTY Lines for SSH Only
steps.instruction: Configure virtual terminal (VTY) lines to accept only SSH connections, rejecting Telnet.
steps.why: VTY lines control remote access. 'transport input ssh' disables Telnet and enables SSH only.
steps.expectedOutput: VTY lines configured for SSH only
hints: Use 'line vty 0 4' to configure all VTY lines
'transport input ssh' allows only SSH, blocking Telnet

commonMistakes.solution: Ensure 'transport input ssh' is set, not 'transport input all'

steps.title: Create Local User Account
steps.instruction: Create a local user with privilege level 15 (full access) and a secure password for SSH authentication.
steps.why: SSH with 'login local' requires user accounts configured on the device. Privilege 15 grants full administrative access.
steps.expectedOutput: User account created

commonMistakes.solution: 'secret' encrypts the password; 'password' stores it in plaintext

steps.title: Enable Local Authentication
steps.instruction: Configure VTY lines to use the local user database for authentication instead of a remote AAA server.
steps.why: 'login local' tells the device to check the locally configured username/password database.
steps.expectedOutput: Local authentication enabled
hints: Ensure username is configured before testing

steps.title: Verify SSH Hardening Complete
steps.instruction: Verify the SSH configuration is complete and Telnet has been disabled. Test that SSH access works.
steps.why: Final verification ensures the hardening is effective and SSH access is functional.
steps.expectedOutput: SSH v2 enabled, RSA keys present, VTY configured for SSH only
hints: Use 'show ip ssh' to verify SSH settings
Use 'show ssh' to see active SSH connections
Use 'show line' to verify VTY configuration

learningObjectives: Understand why SSH is more secure than Telnet
Configure hostname and domain-name for SSH
Generate RSA crypto keys for SSH
Configure VTY lines to accept only SSH
Create local user accounts for authentication
prerequisites: Understanding of network device access methods
explanation: This lab teaches SSH hardening by configuring a network device to use SSH v2 instead of insecure Telnet. You will configure crypto keys, restrict VTY access, and create local user accounts.
finalVerification: SSH v2 is enabled, Telnet is disabled, and SSH connections are accepted with local authentication
